alignments.note: Jehovah is the written subject of the whole series, and the ASV resumes it with He at the head of the third colon, so both realizations belong to this noun's one discontinuous unit (rule 25), headed on the first English occurrence. The accepted alignment gave He to the participle מוֹרִיד, but rule 25 states flatly that rule 17's permission reaches a pronoun realizing a finite verb's own person and number and that a participle in a verbless clause takes only the copula. The competing reading marks He added under rule 20's closing sentence, which rule 25 excludes wherever the verse writes the nominal.
Participial predicate; the subject is written separately.
Light verb plus complement; head on the complement carrying the lexeme (rule 44).
Participial predicate with its phrasal particle; down alone names nothing, so the head stays on the verb (rule 44). The subject pronoun is the written Jehovah's under rule 25.
Supplied to for the goal accusative belongs to the noun (rule 33).
Phrasal particle up stays with the finite verb (rule 44).

review_notes: Corrected: the supplied He at t006 is the written יְהוָה's second realization under rule 25, not the participle's subject pronoun; a participle in a verbless clause takes only the copula.
bringeth down and bringeth up are read as verb plus particle rather than verb plus complement, on rule 44's own subtraction: down and up alone name nothing.
